evidence: Reviewed all non-generated source/config for static/shared data, Task/Thread APIs, singleton factories, locks, monitors, concurrent collections, transaction boundaries, service-instance behavior and optimistic concurrency metadata. WCF requests share LocalDB regardless of distinct DbContext instances. Source shows manual key generation with DatabaseGeneratedOption.None and no atomic read/allocate transaction. Several checklist findings describe overlapping aspects of the same key-allocation race, not separate independent bugs. Excluded singleton observations are not counted as application vulnerabilities. No load/concurrency test executed.
Assessment execution duration was not measured; execution_time_seconds is null rather than a fabricated duration.

Refinement: CWE-543 and CWE-821 are NOT_FOUND. Singleton.cs:6-15 uses ConcurrentDictionary.GetOrAdd, whose factory may run more than once, but this helper is excluded from eShopWinForms.csproj Compile items and no concurrent production caller or constructor-side-effect resource was established. Hypothetical concurrent creation does not establish the required application multithreaded context.

Overlap accounting: CWE-567, CWE-662, CWE-667 and CWE-820 describe ONE root cause at CatalogService.svc.cs:65-70: unprotected read-maximum/increment/insert allocation of shared database keys. CWE-667 denotes absent protective locking for this exclusive operation, not a separately observed lock-release defect. Count four checklist matches, but one independent concurrency issue; EF write transaction/primary-key enforcement does not serialize the earlier allocation read.

values.name: Use of Singleton Pattern Without Synchronization in a Multithreaded Context
values.description: The product uses the singleton pattern when creating a resource within a multithreaded environment.

values.name: Unsynchronized Access to Shared Data in a Multithreaded Context
values.description: The product does not properly synchronize shared data, such as static variables across threads, which can lead to undefined behavior and unpredictable data changes.

evidence.explanation: Independent WCF requests share the CatalogItems database table. CreateCatalogItem reads the current maximum key and later inserts max+1 without synchronizing that shared allocation state; overlapping requests can choose the same primary key and one SaveChanges fails. Per-service-instance serialization does not serialize different instances against the same table. Overlap: this is the same key-allocation race recorded under CWE-567/CWE-662/CWE-667/CWE-820, not an additional independent vulnerability.

values.name: Improper Synchronization
values.description: The product utilizes multiple threads or processes to allow temporary access to a shared resource that can only be exclusive to one process at a time, but it does not properly synchronize these actions, which might cause simultaneous accesses of this resource by multiple threads or processes.

evidence.explanation: CreateCatalogItem performs a read-maximum/increment/insert operation on shared, manually assigned database keys without an atomic allocation operation or enclosing serializing transaction. Concurrent requests can both obtain the same maximum before either insert commits, producing a primary-key collision. SaveChanges atomicity does not cover the preceding Max query. Overlap: this is the same key-allocation race recorded under CWE-567/CWE-662/CWE-667/CWE-820, not an additional independent vulnerability.

values.name: Improper Locking
values.description: The product does not properly acquire or release a lock on a resource, leading to unexpected resource state changes and behaviors.

evidence.explanation: The exclusive key-allocation critical section in CreateCatalogItem has no lock/serializable transaction protecting the Max query through insertion. Locks taken only for the later database write do not prevent competing callers from selecting the same next key. This is absent protective locking for an inherently exclusive operation, not a lock-release/deadlock claim. Overlap: this is the same key-allocation race recorded under CWE-567/CWE-662/CWE-667/CWE-820, not an additional independent vulnerability.

values.name: Missing Synchronization
values.description: The product utilizes a shared resource in a concurrent manner but does not attempt to synchronize access to the resource.

evidence.explanation: CreateCatalogItem accesses shared database key state concurrently but makes no synchronization attempt around Max(i => i.Id), ++maxId and Add/SaveChanges. Two callers can calculate the same next Id; the database uniqueness constraint detects the collision only after the race and the service has no retry path. Overlap: this is the same key-allocation race recorded under CWE-567/CWE-662/CWE-667/CWE-820, not an additional independent vulnerability.

values.name: Incorrect Synchronization
values.description: The product utilizes a shared resource in a concurrent manner, but it does not correctly synchronize access to the resource.

result.finding: Assessed 6 CWE rules in Concurrency & Synchronization: 4 FOUND, 2 NOT_FOUND
